one_liner: Benchmark repo: Rust faer CSR SpMV and Lanczos exp(-A)b beat Eigen on one core but lose to oneMKL and PETSc.
what_it_does: Companion benchmark for the arXiv preprint 2606.19213 (Lombardo and Durastante, University of Pisa). On one pinned core it times y += A*x on 28 SuiteSparse matrices, and one-pass and two-pass Lanczos evaluation of exp(-A)b on 15 symmetric matrices. faer (Rust, upstream CSC plus a CSR path in the authors' fork) runs against Eigen, PETSc, oneMKL inspector-executor and PSBLAS through C, C++ and Fortran FFI wrappers. It is a harness, not a library: the reusable parts are the faer fork (codeberg.org/lukefleed/faer, used through faer's sparse_dense_matmul and SparseRowMat API) and the Rust Lanczos code in src/lanczos (lanczos_into with a caller-owned LanczosWorkspace).
how_it_is_fast: The Rust SpMV is faer's sparse_dense_matmul with Accum::Add and Par::Seq. According to src/lib.rs, faer 0.24 reinterprets a CSR matrix as a transposed CSC matrix and dispatches to dense_sparse_csc_matmul, giving one dot product per row; the fork specialises that CSR path, but its code and the paper's analysis could not be read here (Codeberg and arXiv blocked). It is built with fat LTO, codegen-units=1 and target-cpu=native (AVX-512 on Sapphire Rapids). The Eigen 3.4.0 row-major kernel it beats is a single-accumulator scalar loop (Eigen 5.0 uses two accumulators), and the Eigen SpMV wrapper also pays for a temporary vector (see gotchas). In Lanczos, the Rust recurrence fuses w -= beta*v_prev with the alpha dot product into one pass over the vectors and reuses preallocated workspaces.
when_to_use: You need reference numbers for single-core Rust sparse kernels against C, C++ and Fortran libraries on standard SuiteSparse matrices, with code, flags and CPU stated.
You already use faer in Rust and need CSR SpMV: the fork's faer/csr is 1.11x faster than faer/csc (geomean, 21 of 28 matrices) and 1.12x faster than Eigen CSR (19 of 28), derived from summary.csv.

Memory-bound Krylov matrix-function evaluation (exp(-A)b) where the basis does not fit: the two-pass Lanczos keeps O(n) storage at twice the SpMV count, and the Rust version is 1.04x Eigen and 1.11x PSBLAS here.

You want a template for fair cross-language benchmarking: build.rs checks that clang's LLVM major matches rustc's for cross-language LTO, setup stays outside the timed loop, and Criterion runs 50 samples over 100 s.
when_not_to_use: Fastest single-core CSR SpMV on x86: oneMKL inspector-executor is 1.24x faster (faer wins 4 of 28) and PETSc MatMultAdd 1.23x faster (5 of 28); per-matrix PETSc ratios run from 0.54x to 1.47x.
Lanczos where PETSc is an option: PETSc is 1.19x faster one-pass (faer wins 2 of 15) and 1.22x faster two-pass (4 of 15).
Multi-threaded or distributed SpMV: everything is Par::Seq on one taskset-pinned core, and there are no parallel results.
You need a dependency you can ship: there is no LICENSE file (only license = "MIT" in Cargo.toml), the kernel lives in an unreleased git fork pinned to commit 009ac1eb, and nightly Rust is required.
Machines without Spack: build.rs hard-requires spack-located LLVM 22, GCC 14.3.0, oneMKL, PETSc, Eigen, PSBLAS and OpenMPI, even for cargo check.

integration.form: source-drop (benchmark repo); the Rust kernel comes in as a git dependency on a faer fork
integration.dependencies: faer fork (git codeberg.org/lukefleed/faer, commit 009ac1eb, features std and nightly), matrix-market-rs, criterion; baselines via Spack: intel-oneapi-mkl, PETSc (linked to MKL), Eigen, PSBLAS develop, OpenMPI, OpenBLAS, LLVM 22, GCC 14.3.0
integration.min_toolchain: Rust nightly-2026-04-14 (edition 2024, faer nightly feature); clang from LLVM 22 to match rustc's LLVM for cross-language LTO; gfortran 14.3.0
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux as tested (Sapphire Rapids, Spack target sapphirerapids, -march=native); others not documented
integration.thread_safety: single-threaded by design (Par::Seq, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, mkl_sequential); otherwise not documented

gotchas: Eigen SpMV baseline flaw: ffi/spmv/eigen.cpp runs '*(ctx->y) += A * x' without .noalias(). In both Eigen 3.4.0 and 5.0.0, evaluator_assume_aliasing<Product<Lhs, Rhs, DefaultProduct>> is true and call_assignment builds a plain temporary ('tmp(src)') before adding it. So each Eigen call allocates, fills and re-reads an nrows-long vector that the faer, PETSc MatMultAdd and MKL paths do not pay. The Eigen Lanczos wrappers do use .noalias(), and the Eigen gap shrinks there from 1.12x to 1.04x; the cost was confirmed in source, not measured. The missing -DNDEBUG matters less, because Eigen's sparse inner loop calls coeff(), which has only an internal assert.

The Lanczos rows compare implementations as well as languages: the Rust recurrence (src/lanczos/algorithms/mod.rs) fuses w -= beta*v_prev with the alpha dot product, while the Eigen wrapper makes separate passes. On the MKL side, mkl_sparse_set_mv_hint is commented out in ffi/spmv/mkl.c, so MKL optimises without a call-count hint and still wins.

Baseline library versions are not recorded: spack.yaml leaves eigen, petsc and intel-oneapi-mkl unpinned, psblas@develop tracks a branch, and no spack.lock is committed. Which Eigen ran (3.4.x with a one-accumulator loop, or 5.0.x with two) is unknown. The eigen.cpp header comment says -ffast-math, but build.rs has that flag commented out on every wrapper.

The CSR specialisation behind the faer/csr rows is in the Codeberg fork, not in this repo or upstream faer, and could not be inspected here; x is all ones and y accumulates across iterations by design (bench comment: values do not affect a memory-bound kernel).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling in this category covers sparse SpMV or Krylov methods (TriangularSolve.jl and Gaius.jl are dense, Clarabel.rs is a conic solver). Use upstream faer (catalogued separately as sarah-quinones/faer-rs) as the dependency, and this repo to reproduce or extend the Rust-versus-C/C++ sparse comparison.
verified_claims_summary: On one taskset-pinned core of a Xeon Gold 6418H (Criterion, 50 samples, 100 s window), faer/csr built with rustc nightly-2026-04-14 (fat LTO, target-cpu=native) was compared against wrappers built with clang 22 -O3 -march=native -flto and Spack-built PETSc, oneMKL (sequential) and PSBLAS. Geomean SpMV over 28 SuiteSparse matrices: 1.12x faster than Eigen CSR and 1.20x faster than Eigen CSC, parity with PSBLAS CSR (1.02x), but 0.81x of oneMKL CSR and 0.82x of PETSc CSR. Lanczos exp(-A)b: 1.04x Eigen and 0.84x PETSc one-pass, 1.04x Eigen and 0.82x PETSc two-pass. All re-derived here from python/data/summary.csv.
status_note: Research companion repo (58 commits, last 2026-06-18, 4 stars, no releases) with no LICENSE file, so reference use only. Reproducing it needs nightly Rust, an unreleased faer fork on Codeberg and a full Spack HPC stack. The Rust-beats-Eigen result is partly a harness artifact (the Eigen SpMV wrapper builds a temporary on every call), and Rust loses to oneMKL and PETSc throughout.
